problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a set of sensitive electronic components onto identical transport pallets for shipment. The components are as follows:

* Component Alpha: 54 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Beta: 31 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Gamma: 45 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Delta: 35 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Epsilon: 49 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Zeta: 36 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Eta: 41 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Theta: 38 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Iota: 58 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Kappa: 30 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Lambda: 53 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Mu: 63 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Nu: 56 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Xi: 37 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Omicron: 63 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Pi: 45 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Rho: 61 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Sigma: 48 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Tau: 47 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Upsilon: 55 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Phi: 57 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Chi: 60 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Psi: 33 units of volumetric displacement
* Component Omega: 40 units of volumetric displacement

Each pallet is certified to support a maximum total volumetric displacement of 100 units. The objective is to assign every component to a pallet, with no component split across multiple pallets, such that the cumulative displacement on any pallet does not surpass its certified limit. The coordinator seeks to complete this allocation utilizing the smallest possible number of pallets.
